author: TEDx Talks
description:
Ever smiled and nodded even though you missed what was said? This candid exploration reveals why this survival tactic sabotages relationships and how honest communication creates deeper connections for everyone, hearing or not. 

Gael Hannan is an advocate, author, and speaker on hearing loss. Born with progressive hearing loss, she now uses both a hearing aid and cochlear implant. Becoming a mother at 40 led her to discover a passion for advocacy. For 30 years, she has created award-winning programs blending comedy and drama to help others navigate hearing loss. A globally recognized writer, she authored The Way I Hear It and Hear & Beyond. Gael has served on national and international accessibility organizations. She lives in North Saanich, Vancouver Island, with her husband, “The Hearing Husband,” cherishing visits from their four children and seven grandchildren. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community.
title: How to communicate better with hearing loss | Gael Hannan | TEDxVictoria

author: TEDx Talks
description: This powerful TEDx talk by Riddhima Dabral shines a light on the silent reality of mental health struggles that go unseen, unheard, and too often dismissed. Beginning with a friend’s haunting confession—“I wish I had a fracture instead of anxiety”—she unpacks why society offers empathy to visible pain but judgment to invisible suffering. Through compelling stories and sharp experiments that reveal our hidden biases, Riddhima challenges the way we casually ask “How are you?” and how rarely we stay for the real answer. With honesty and emotional depth, she shows that awareness means nothing without empathy, presence, and the courage to create spaces where it’s safe to say “I’m not okay.” This talk is a profound invitation to rethink how we listen, how we respond, and how we begin to understand the pain we cannot see. Riddhima Dabral is a passionate Humanities student from Vivekanand School with a strong interest in psychology and mental health. A state-level Delhi Yoga Championship winn
title: When Pain Becomes Invisible | Riddhima Dabral | TEDxVivekanandSchool

description:
ในวัย 41 ปี สิงห์-วรรณสิงห์ ประเสริฐกุล เลือกเดินทางสู่สมรภูมิอันตรายทั่วโลกพร้อมกระเป๋ากล้องกว่า 25 กิโลกรัม ด้านในบรรจุเลนส์หลายระยะที่ทำให้เขาสำรวจรอยร้าวผ่านสงครามชัดเจนขึ้น เขามองเห็นความขัดแย้งตั้งแต่ระดับปัจเจกจนถึงมนุษยชาติ และตั้งคำถามว่าอะไรคือรอยร้าวแท้จริงที่สงครามทิ้งไว้ และอะไรคือสิ่งที่มนุษย์ยังคงทำได้ ในโลกกว้างใหญ่ที่สงครามเป็นเพียงกลไกหนึ่งในวัฏจักรของโลกใบนี้เท่านั้น

At the age of 41, Wannasingh Prasertkul chooses to journey into some of the world’s most dangerous conflict zones, carrying over 25 kilograms of camera equipment. Inside his bag are lenses of various ranges tools that allow him to examine the fractures left by war with greater clarity.

He witnesses conflict from the individual to the scale of humanity, and asks what war truly leaves behind and what humans can still choose to do in response, in a world where war is only one force within a much larger cycle. ในวัย 41 ปี สิงห์-วรรณสิงห์ ประเสริฐกุล เลือกเดินทางสู่สมรภูมิอันตรายทั่วโลกพร้อมกระเป๋ากล้องกว่

การแสดงชุดนี้จะพาเราดำดิ่งลงไปฟังเสียงของโลกผ่านการเคลื่อนไหวของร่างกาย จังหวะ และแรงสั่นสะเทือนจากทีม RAWR โดยได้รับแรงบันดาลใจจากองค์ความรู้ของ ศ.ดร.สันติ ภัยหลบลี้ นักธรณีวิทยาผู้เป็นตัวกลางสื่อสารระหว่างมนุษย์และโลกใบนี้

Earthquakes are not humanity’s enemy. They are proof that the Earth is still breathing.

As we live our lives on the surface, the world beneath us moves in quiet rhythm shifting, balancing, and renewing itself in its own time.

This performance invites us to dive deep and listen to the Earth’s voice through movement, rhythm, and vibration, brought to life by the RAWR team. It is inspired by the knowledge and insights of Professor Dr. Santi Phailoblee, a geologist who serves as a bridge between humanity and the living planet we call home. เพราะแผ่นดินไหวไม่ใช่ศัตรูของมนุษย์ หากแต

author: TEDx Talks
description: Plutôt que de chercher à rendre Mars viable, osons regarder en face le déséquilibre à l’origine des crises sur Terre. En renversant les perspectives et en s’appuyant sur des études et des faits, Marie Eloy démontre que la solution est déjà là, sous nos yeux. Efficace, documentée et pourtant ignorée, cette ressource est capable de transformer l’économie, de protéger le vivant et de renforcer la paix, au bénéfice de toutes et tous. Cette conférence pragmatique et porteuse d’espoir montre comment agir, dès maintenant, pour activer cette solution et envisager, enfin, un avenir durable pour l’humanité. Le sursaut attendu pour passer à l’action !  Ancienne journaliste à RFI, autrice de « les femmes sauveront elles le monde, » fondatrice des réseaux Femmes des Territoires, Bouge ta Boite et conférencière internationale, Marie Eloy consacre son énergie à fédérer et à rassembler pour que la mixité puisse agir et transformer le monde… en mieux ! Distinguée à plusieurs reprises par Forbes et par
title: Et si la solution aux crises mondiales était là depuis toujours ? | Marie Eloy | TEDxMontmartre

description: Most people think AI is only for engineers, coders, or tech geniuses—but that couldn’t be further from the truth. In this video, we break down Generative AI in the simplest way possible, showing how it already fits into your everyday life—whether you’re a student, parent, working professional, or business owner. No jargon. No complicated explanations. Just real examples of how AI can help you save time, think better, learn faster, and make everyday tasks easier. If you use a smartphone, send emails, study, create content, or make decisions at work, this video is for you. By the end, you’ll realize that AI isn’t something to fear—it’s a tool you can start using today to make life simpler, smarter, and more productive. Dr. Pritam Sahoo is a Google Cloud Partner Architect, AI educator with over 19 years of global experience across Google, Oracle, SAP, and Flexera. Jasmine King shares her journey through dating apps, heartbreak, and rejection, revealing the lessons she’s learned about self-worth, boundaries, and loving the person who’s always there: you. Jasmine is a dedicated Sexual Wellness Advocate committed to fostering safe, empowering spaces for open conversations about sexual health and relationships. Through her advocacy, she encourages honest dialogue as a pathway to education and informed decision-making. By bringing these conversations into the light, she reminds individuals that no one navigates love or intimacy alone. “你居住的城市，值得被好好看见。”

张丽珠创办《城视报》，一份在槟城坚持十一年的社区杂志，不追逐热点，只专注记录城市被忽略的细节。从街头诗、老招牌到平民区与被遗忘的岛屿，《城视报》像一面镜子，映照出城市的人情与记忆。

面对 AI 写稿、短视频盛行的时代，他们依然选择 “慢”——让杂志走进展览、课程与导览，把纸上的故事带到街头巷尾。

张丽珠相信，记录城市，不只是记者的任务，每个人都可以成为见证者，因为 “城市的每一个角落，都值得留下痕迹。”

“The city you call home deserves to be truly seen.”

description: What does it take to save a life with one organ? In this talk, Prof. Dr. Ramesh Singh Bhandari shares his journey from a young medical student to becoming one of Nepal’s pioneering liver transplant surgeons. He takes the audience behind the operating room doors, revealing the relentless training, high-stakes decisions, and human stories that shape every transplant. Beyond surgical skill, he reflects on the courage, empathy, and perseverance required to transform patients’ lives—and an entire healthcare system. This talk is both a personal story of dedication and a testament to what is possible when passion meets purpose, inspiring anyone who dreams of making a difference in medicine or life. Prof. Dr. Ramesh Singh Bhandari is a pioneering liver transplant surgeon in Nepal and Professor of Surgery at the Institute of Medicine, Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital (TUTH). Born in Baitadi, he studied MBBS at BPKIHS, completed MS in Surgery at TUTH, and later specialized in GI and HPB s
title: The Making of a Liver Transplant Surgeon | Prof. Dr. Ramesh Singh Bhandari | TEDxIOM

author: TEDx Talks
description: Inga, a coral reef scientist, addresses the urgent threats to coral reefs from local and global stressors, emphasising the interconnectedness of species reliant on these ecosystems. She advocates for collective action and making informed consumer choices, fostering hope amid mounting climate change challenges. Her passionate message encourages a shared responsibility to protect these vital ecosystems for future generations. Inga is an Assistant Professor at Lingnan University and a coral reef scientist with a PhD from the University of Hong Kong. Over the last decade, she has conducted research on marine and terrestrial mutualisms—partnerships between species. Her work focuses on diverse biological systems, including corals with algal partners and plants with mycorrhizal fungi, to understand their evolution. Inga also addresses urgent threats to coral reefs and advocates for collective action to protect these vital ecosystems for future generations. This talk was given at a TEDx event
title: What coral reefs teach us about survival | Dr. Inga Conti-Jerpe | TEDxTinHauWomen

In this joint talk, Emily, a trauma therapist, and Shulin, a passionate student podcaster, explore the emotional toll of feeling unheard. They share personal experiences showcasing the importance of creating safe spaces for expression. Advocating for compassionate listening and acceptance, they aim to transform self-doubt into understanding, demonstrating how true connection can heal emotional wounds and foster resilience. Emily, a National Certified Counsellor and trauma therapist, helps individuals recover from trauma, depression, and anxiety. Early NGO work in Washington, D.C., combating human trafficking, inspired her to pursue advanced trauma-focused training. She now serves at the Hong Kong Dignity Institute, offering programmes for refugees, survivors of trafficking, and those affected by abuse. In a joint talk with Shulin Ho, Emily advocates for compassionate listening to heal emotional wounds and foster resilience.

title: The Healing Power of Being Heard | Emily Kusunoki & Shulin 何書凌 Ho | TEDxTinHauWomen

From Ancient Egypt to dazzling quick changes in London’s West End, and their modern-day empowerment for those battling hair loss, Katie showcases how wigs offer the freedom to redefine one’s identity and embrace possibilities of self-expression. Katie is an accomplished hair and make-up artist with over 15 years of experience transforming characters for stage and screen. Her career has taken her from London's West End to Netflix productions. She specialises in styling and creating elaborate period wigs, weaving history and creativity into her work. Katie is dedicated to using her skills to empower individuals facing hair loss. In her talk, she explores the historical and transformative power of wigs as a symbol of identity and self-expression. Together, their music becomes a conversation across generations and a reminder that the blues have always been shaped by those on the margins. Opening video footage courtesy of Bill Weaver. Daniel Morel is a Montreal-born harmonicist and blues musician who busked across Canada before settling in Victoria. With a style shaped by street performance and blues legends, he delivers gritty, soulful shows that reflect his resilience, journey, and deep love for music.

description:
To nie jest trudne dlatego, że jesteś niekompetentny, ale dlatego, że Twój mózg robi to po raz pierwszy!
Najlepszy moment do działania jest dokładnie teraz. Posłuchaj, Aleksandry i dowiedz się, dlaczego warto przestać odkładać życie na później i jak odwaga do wykonania pierwszego kroku wiele  zmienia. Jej marzeniem jest zostanie kardiochirurgiem i niesienie pomocy w krajach objętych konfliktem zbrojnym, łącząc pasję do nauki z realnym działaniem na rzecz innych.

W 2024 roku została wyróżniona na liście 10 najlepszych młodych mówców w Polsce. W wolnym czasie trenuje do survivalowych biegów terenowych, konsekwentnie sprawdzając swoje granice i udowadniając, że najlepszy moment na działanie jest zawsze teraz. author: TEDx Talks
description: How might we elevate our days, strengthen health and optimism, and somehow build a better world for others and the planet? Research in the fields of positive and environmental psychology demonstrates that activation of a character strength, known as Appreciation of Beauty and Excellence, accomplishes all that. Maria Sirois, Psy.D. has spent more than three decades in the boardrooms of business, bedsides of the dying and everywhere in between to do one thing: offer the data, stories, tools and perspectives that enable us to cultivate resilience, health, wisdom and a greater capacity to lead ourselves and others well, no matter the strain or suffering of the moment. As a resilience expert, positive psychologist and international consultant, she is known for her authenticity, wisdom and compassion. She is the author of three books: the newly released, The Generous Exchange: How Attention to Beauty, Goodness and Excellence Restores Us and Our World, A Short Course in Happiness After Loss
title: Could beauty save the world? | Maria Sirois | TEDxBerkshires

author: TEDx Talks
description:
16歳で家族と離れ、里親や児童養護施設との出会いを通して人生が大きく動き出した土濃塚達也の実体験。虐待や貧困により施設で育つ子どもたちが、18歳で直面する「仕事」と「住まい」の壁。その現実に向き合い、就労と居場所を一体で支える支援を実践しています。諦めなければ、どんな環境からでも未来はつくれる。その可能性を社会全体で支えるための挑戦を語ります。

At age 16, Tatsuya Donozuka left his family behind. His life took a major turn through encounters with foster parents and children's homes. Children raised in institutions due to abuse or poverty face the dual barriers of “work” and “housing” when they turn 18. Confronting this reality, we practice support that integrates employment support and a safe place to live. If you don't give up, you can build a future from any environment. He share our challenge to support this possibility as a society.
